blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. and Education Secretary Sonny Angara spearheaded the Visayas leg of the government’s nationwide digital modernization campaign on Friday, turning over an initial batch of 300 MacBook Neo laptops to public school educators in Iloilo City. According to a statement from the Department of Education (DepEd), the turnover, held at Mabini Elementary School in Iloilo City, marks the expanding reach of the DepEd Computerization Program (DCP), which aims to bridge long-standing digital divides across the country’s public schools. “This is part of our broader efforts to improve the quality of education in our country.
